Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the demo last week. Before procurement can finalize terms we need to confirm a few technical/legal points about your EU-only processing offering and the SCCs/operator language. High level asks:

- Does Redwood perform any inference or model-hosted transformations outside the EU for HealthNova customer content? If yes, which components and under what conditions?
- Is the control plane (metadata, routing, billing) hosted outside the EU? What data elements are included and are they pseudonymized?
- Do backups or DR replicas ever leave EU boundaries? If so we need to understand the retention window and access controls.
- Can Redwood provide an 'operator' annex to the SCCs that restricts personnel access, entitlements, and requires EU-based operator access only for this customer?

We have a procurement deadline of Fri 11 Mar and legal will need an attestation or an explicit statement we can include in the purchase order. Also please attach any short runbook or diagram showing the data flow and where stewarded keys live.

Best,

Diane —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary of Redwood's current default and the configurable options we can offer for HealthNova. Attaching two short artifacts: a one-page operations flow and a draft operator annex for SCCs.

1) Default hosted offering (what typically happens today)
- Inference: customer input (prompts/content) is processed in eu-west-1 (GCP) when the customer selects EU region. Model weights and runtime stay in-region for inference execution.
- Control plane: metadata required for orchestration (request routing, billing meter points, metrics) is hosted in our central control plane (US region). That metadata is pseudonymized: we strip direct identifiers and use a hashed tenant id and request id. No raw customer payload is retained in the control plane.
- Backups/DR: snapshot backups of customer model caches and config are replicated to an EU-only backup storage by default; we maintain a secondary replica in our US DR region for catastrophic restore. Replication to the US is encrypted in transit and at rest; access requires elevated approval and is logged.

2) Stronger contractual commitments / optional configuration for HealthNova (what we can deliver as part of a Dedicated/Private or tightened Hosted contract)
- EU-exclusive processing: we can configure your account so that both inference and control-plane telemetry for HealthNova are routed only to EU regions (control plane regionalization). This includes preventing automatic replication of backups to non-EU DR except under documented emergency conditions with prior written consent.
- Operator access restrictions: we will include an operator annex to the SCCs that limits human operator access to named roles, requires MFA + bastion access from EU IP ranges where possible, and requires access justification + recorded session logs.
- Key custody: Customer-managed KMS (Bring Your Own Key) in your EU project can be enforced; Redwood will never persist the plaintext material and will require KMS approval for key usage.

3) Evidence and timeline
- We can provide: (a) SCCs with operator annex (draft attached), (b) ops flow diagram showing region boundaries (attached), and (c) an attestation letter on company letterhead confirming configuration options.
- Estimated delivery: draft annex + ops flow (attached) now; signed attestation template within 10 business days after legal review. If you require an explicit signed statement that Redwood "will not transfer or process HealthNova user content outside the EU" we need to lock in the EU-exclusive configuration and agree to limited exception handling for DR — we will confirm precise wording in the annex.

Next steps: tell us whether HealthNova needs EU-exclusive control plane or the standard pseudonymized control plane, and whether you require backup replication to the US for DR. We can then populate the annex and attestation with customer-specific commitments.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai

Diane / team — quick internal add from ops before finalizing wording.

- Control plane data: to be explicit, telemetry includes timing, model id, token counts, and hashed tenant id. We will commit to removing any free-text logs that could contain customer content from the control plane retention for HealthNova on request and to reduce retention to 30 days for that telemetry.
- Backups & restore: our EU-primary backups are 30-day rolling snapshots; the US replica is cold and only promoted under declared DR. We will document the DR activation process in the annex and require HealthNova sign-off for any cross-border restore.
- Erasure: if HealthNova triggers an erasure request, we will remove active data and schedule snapshot zeroization; full proof of deletion for snapshots may require a short ops window (we will provide certificate-of-destruction details in the annex).
